english: $$f(x)=\begin{cases}-\dfrac{x}{8}, & x<0\\ x^{2}-x+\dfrac{1}{2}, & 0\le x\le 1\\ \dfrac{3}{2}-x, & x>1\end{cases}\qquad g(x)=\begin{cases}x+1, & x<\tfrac{1}{4}\\ 2x, & x\ge \tfrac{1}{4}\end{cases}$$

Let $h:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $h(x)=g(f(x))$, and let $S$ be the set of all points of $\mathbb{R}$ at which $h$ is NOT differentiable. Then the sum of all the elements of $S$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ तथा $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ इस प्रकार परिभाषित हैं
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}-\dfrac{x}{8}, & x<0\\ x^{2}-x+\dfrac{1}{2}, & 0\le x\le 1\\ \dfrac{3}{2}-x, & x>1\end{cases}\qquad g(x)=\begin{cases}x+1, & x<\tfrac{1}{4}\\ 2x, & x\ge \tfrac{1}{4}\end{cases}$$
माना $h:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $h(x)=g(f(x))$ द्वारा परिभाषित है, तथा $S$, $\mathbb{R}$ के उन सभी बिन्दुओं का समुच्चय है जिन पर $h$ अवकलनीय नहीं है। तब $S$ के सभी अवयवों का योग ______ है।
solution: $g$ changes form only at $f(x)=\dfrac14$, so split by the sign of $f(x)-\dfrac14$
$x<0$: $f=-\dfrac x8<\dfrac14\iff x>-2$; so $h=-\dfrac x4$ for $x\le-2$ and $h=1-\dfrac x8$ for $-2<x<0$
$0\le x\le1$: $f=\left(x-\dfrac12\right)^{2}+\dfrac14\ge\dfrac14$, so $h=2x^{2}-2x+1$ (at $x=\dfrac12$ $f$ only touches $\dfrac14$, so $h$ stays smooth)
$x=0$: $f$ jumps ($0$ to $\dfrac12$) but $h(0^-)=1=h(0)$, so $h$ is continuous; slopes $-\dfrac18$ and $-2$ differ, not differentiable
$x=1$: $h=1$ from both sides; slopes $2$ and $-2$, not differentiable
solution_full: The rule for $g(t)$ changes only at $t=\dfrac14$, and $g$ is discontinuous there ($g(\tfrac14^-)=\dfrac54$, $g(\tfrac14)=\dfrac12$). So $h=g\circ f$ can fail to be smooth only where $f$ changes its rule ($x=0$, $x=1$) or where $f(x)$ crosses $\dfrac14$.
For $x<0$: $f(x)=-\dfrac x8>0$ and $f(x)<\dfrac14\iff x>-2$. Hence $h(x)=2f(x)=-\dfrac x4$ for $x\le-2$ and $h(x)=f(x)+1=1-\dfrac x8$ for $-2<x<0$.

For $0\le x\le1$: $f(x)=x^{2}-x+\dfrac12=\left(x-\dfrac12\right)^{2}+\dfrac14\ge\dfrac14$, with equality only at $x=\dfrac12$. So $h(x)=2f(x)=2x^{2}-2x+1$ on the whole interval. At $x=\dfrac12$ the value of $f$ touches $\dfrac14$ from above and never goes below it, so $h$ uses the same rule on both sides and is differentiable there.
For $x>1$: $f(x)=\dfrac32-x$, and $f(x)\ge\dfrac14\iff x\le\dfrac54$. So $h(x)=2f(x)=3-2x$ on $\left(1,\dfrac54\right]$ and $h(x)=f(x)+1=\dfrac52-x$ for $x>\dfrac54$.
At $x=-2$: $h(-2)=\dfrac12$ and $\lim_{x\to-2^-}h(x)=\dfrac12$, but $\lim_{x\to-2^+}h(x)=1+\dfrac14=\dfrac54$. So $h$ is discontinuous, hence not differentiable, at $-2$.

At $x=0$: $f$ itself is discontinuous ($f(0^-)=0$, $f(0)=\dfrac12$), yet $\lim_{x\to0^-}h(x)=1$ and $h(0)=2\cdot\dfrac12=1=\lim_{x\to0^+}h(x)$, so $h$ is continuous at $0$. The left derivative is $-\dfrac18$ and the right derivative is $4x-2\big|_{x=0}=-2$, so $h$ is not differentiable at $0$.
At $x=1$: $h(1)=1$ and $\lim_{x\to1^+}(3-2x)=1$, so $h$ is continuous; the left derivative is $4x-2\big|_{x=1}=2$ and the right derivative is $-2$, so $h$ is not differentiable at $1$.
At $x=\dfrac54$: $h\left(\dfrac54\right)=\dfrac12$ and the left limit is $\dfrac12$, but the right limit is $\dfrac52-\dfrac54=\dfrac54$. So $h$ is discontinuous at $\dfrac54$.
Every piece of $h$ is a polynomial, so $h$ is differentiable at all other points, including $x=\dfrac12$.
Hence $S=\left\{-2,0,1,\dfrac54\right\}$ and the sum of its elements is $-2+0+1+\dfrac54=\dfrac14=0.25$.
originality_note: New: a composite of two piecewise functions in which the outer jump is triggered only where the inner function crosses the jump value, while a tangential touch (x = 1/2) and a jump of the inner function (x = 0) are both healed in the composite (way 5). Closest known: continuity of g(f(x)) for piecewise f and g in JEE Main. Different because: the student must separate crossing from touching and see that a discontinuity of f can disappear in g o f, yet still leave a corner.
stem_review: Read as a student: every set, function and symbol introduced with its domain, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with code and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked each of the six candidate points (-2, 0, 1/2, 1, 5/4 and the junctions) numerically with one-sided limits and difference quotients on a fine grid; only -2, 0, 1, 5/4 fail. The word NOT is capitalised as in JEE. Changed: No change.
key_step: Splitting by the sign of f(x) - 1/4 and checking each junction, noticing that x = 1/2 (touch) is harmless and x = 0 (jump of f) gives a corner but no jump.
justification: A routine chain of piecewise checks with two small traps; no non-routine idea. Below 2023-P2-Q6 (L3), which needs a product with a greatest-integer factor and statement checks; above 2025-P1-Q15 (L1) short parts. Numerical format keeps it at the top of level 2.

concept_use.Composite functions: domain and composit: h = g(f(x)) is written piece by piece by composing the piecewise rules of f and g, splitting at f(x) = 1/4.
concept_use.Continuity and Differentiability of comp: One-sided limits and one-sided derivatives of h at -2, 0, 1 and 5/4 decide continuity and differentiability of the composite.
